summary: This is a reference page for the DROP NETWORK POLICY command, which removes a specified network policy from the system. It explains the syntax (with an optional IF EXISTS clause), the name parameter and its quoting and case-sensitivity rules, and usage notes on ownership, non-recoverability, and assignment restrictions. A single example drops a policy named mypolicy. The surrounding navigation menu and footer boilerplate are ignored.
one_line: Reference for the DROP NETWORK POLICY command, which removes a network policy, its privilege requirements, and restrictions.
key_facts: DROP NETWORK POLICY removes the specified network policy from the system.
Only security administrators (users with the SECURITYADMIN role) can drop network policies.
The syntax is DROP NETWORK POLICY [ IF EXISTS ] <name>.
If the name identifier contains spaces or special characters, the entire string must be enclosed in double quotes.
Identifiers enclosed in double quotes are case-sensitive.
Only the network policy owner (a role with the OWNERSHIP privilege on the network policy) or higher can execute this command.
Dropped network policies cannot be recovered and must be recreated.
A network policy cannot be dropped if it is currently assigned to an account, security integration, or user.
The example DROP NETWORK POLICY mypolicy; drops a network policy named mypolicy.
The page's On this page sections are Syntax, Parameters, Usage notes, and Examples.
